statement: The LangChain Certified Agent Engineer exam covers four equally weighted domains: building, testing, deploying, and monitoring agents.
notes: The local exam guide gives the section blueprint; verify the current guide before booking.

statement: The public exam overview lists 40 multiple-choice questions, a 28-correct passing score, 120 minutes, online proctoring, and 24-month validity.
notes: Exam logistics may change; verify before booking.

statement: LangChain Academy lists five free foundation courses as preparation: LangChain Python, Deep Agents, Reliable Agents, Production Monitoring, and LangSmith Deployment.
notes: Course contents and names are version-sensitive.

statement: LangChain is the agent framework, LangGraph is the agent runtime, and Deep Agents is a higher-level agent harness built on LangChain building blocks and the LangGraph runtime.
notes: Use the layers as a selection model, not as mutually exclusive products.

statement: The official foundation material treats tools, messages, short-term memory, context, middleware, human-in-the-loop, and MCP as build-time agent concerns.
notes: Exact APIs should be checked against current documentation before coding.

statement: The reliable-agent course covers tracing, datasets, experiments, code-based evaluation, LLM-as-judge evaluation, and pairwise evaluation.
notes: Evaluator choice depends on the quality question and available ground truth.

statement: The deployment course covers agent deployment, connections, assistants, memory, and multi-tenant authentication and authorization.
notes: This package models the decisions without claiming a specific hosting topology is always correct.

statement: The monitoring course covers cost, product analytics, latency, errors, quality, security monitoring, alerts, and a capstone.
notes: Monitoring signals must be interpreted together with workload and quality context.

statement: The exam is semi-open-book: the guide whitelists smith.langchain.com, docs.langchain.com, and academy.langchain.com, and disallows general search, AI tools, the docs AI helper, browser automation, second screens, and outside communication.
notes: Do not use this package as a substitute for the official exam guide during exam scheduling or proctoring preparation.

statement: The exam guide assigns 10 questions and 25% of the score to each of Build, Test, Deploy, and Monitor.
notes: Use equal weighting for study allocation unless a newer guide supersedes it.

statement: The Build section focuses on create_agent versus deepagents, middleware, context engineering for long-running agents, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, and sandboxing.
notes: These are exam focus areas, not a claim that every implementation must use all of them.

statement: The Test section focuses on code-based evaluators versus LLM-as-judge, online versus offline evaluators, experiments, evaluator alignment, and adding examples to a dataset.
notes: Evaluator selection still depends on the quality question and available ground truth.

statement: The Deploy section focuses on graph, deployment, revision, assistant, thread, and run terminology; multi-region serving; secret handling; authentication versus authorization; and storage durability.
notes: The guide names the focus areas; deployment behavior remains version- and environment-sensitive.

statement: The Monitor section focuses on reading traces, grouping traces into threads, tracking costs and user sentiment, distinguishing Online Evals from Insights, and alerting.
notes: Monitoring concepts should be practiced with representative traces and workload context.

statement: The guide recommends reviewing the listed Academy courses before the exam, learning docs.langchain.com and LangSmith navigation in advance, and taking the practice exam first; it also describes a two-hour proctored session with a dedicated LangSmith organization.
notes: Exam-day logistics and vendor requirements must be rechecked before scheduling.
